_comment: LV-087 — FROZEN BASELINE of migration checksum duplicates that already existed when the guard was written.
Read by BOTH scripts/db-migrate.mjs (runtime refusal) and scripts/verify-migration-checksum-collision.mjs
(CI guard), so there is exactly one list and the two can never disagree.
WHY THESE ARE NOT FIXED RATHER THAN GRANDFATHERED: both files are already applied on the prod ledger
(_system._schema_migrations). Editing an applied migration breaks its checksum (never-edit-an-applied-
migration), and deleting one deletes ledger history to make a guard green — falsifying the audit trail.
Owner ruling 2026-08-05: do NOT retro-delete the existing duplicates; idempotency made the second run a
no-op. The guard exists to prevent the NEXT one.
Prod carries FOUR duplicate-checksum ledger pairs (876 applied rows / 872 distinct checksums). Only the
pair below still exists as two files on disk; for the other three the duplicate file was renumbered away
and survives in the ledger only, so there is nothing on disk for this guard to see:
Entries are pinned to the EXACT checksum AND the exact sorted filename list. A third file joining this
checksum, or any other pair, is NOT covered and fails. This baseline is append-only by review — adding an
entry means consciously accepting a duplicate, which is the decision the guard is meant to force.

duplicates.reason: Both applied on prod before LV-087. Idempotent (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS), so the second run was a no-op. Cannot be edited (applied checksum) or deleted (ledger history).
